h1: Window cleaning in The Heights of Falconhead
intro: The Heights of Falconhead is the hilltop section of Falconhead in Bee Cave, a small group of homes in the $700K to $1.2M range. CleanzATX cleans the glass from the ground with water fed poles, so no ladders touch the walls.

sections.h2: What The Heights homes are like
paragraphs: The name tells you most of it. This is the high ground inside Falconhead, a small section where the lots sit up on the hill instead of down along the fairways. Homes here are listed from about $700,000 to $1.2 million, and they answer to the Falconhead HOA like the rest of the community. The section is not gated. Since the lots sit up high, the houses tend to be open to wind and weather from more than one side.

Hill Country exteriors are the norm, stucco and limestone, with plenty of glass facing the view. Taller elevations are common on a hillside, and that is where owners start to wonder who is going to reach the upper windows safely.

sections.h2: What The Heights windows deal with
paragraphs: Wind is the main problem on a hilltop. It carries dust and pollen straight at the glass and drives rain sideways, so streaks and dirt marks pile up on the exposed faces. Cedar pollen in the winter and live oak pollen in March and April coat the sills in a yellow green layer. West facing panes pick up afternoon sun, which shows every streak and smudge left behind by a rushed clean.

Our water is filtered through a dual RO, 4 stage system with a DI resin tank, down to about 0 TDS. That means the glass dries clear with no spots and no soap film, even on a windy afternoon. Stucco and limestone get a soft wash rather than pressure.

Water fed poles reach up to three stories from the ground, so a tall hillside wall does not mean a ladder against your house. On the inside, we use drop cloths and ladders with cotton covers where a two story room needs it, and the squeegee work is done by hand. Because this is a small section, we usually fit it into a route through the rest of Falconhead rather than running a separate trip. That keeps scheduling flexible, and quotes come back by text, usually within the hour.
A 3,000 square foot home, as an example, is about $300 for exterior windows and roughly two and a quarter to three hours on site. Doing the inside too at $15 a window lands near $450.

faq.q: Can you reach the tall windows on a hillside house?
faq.a: Yes. Our water fed poles reach up to three stories from the ground, so we clean exterior glass without putting ladders against your walls. Interior two story windows are handled with covered ladders and drop cloths.

faq.q: Why do hilltop windows look so streaky?
faq.a: Wind pushes dust and rain into the glass at an angle, and afternoon sun then bakes the marks in. Pure water cleaning leaves no film behind, so the glass looks even when the sun hits it.

faq.q: Do you soft wash limestone here?
faq.a: We do, and it is the only method we use on limestone. Pressure washing can pit the stone. The 12V soft wash system cleans it without that risk.
Exterior windows are $10 each or about $0.10 per square foot, with a $200 minimum. Add the interior at $15 a window if you want both sides. A typical home runs about $350.

faq.q: Is an HOA approval needed for window cleaning?
faq.a: You do not need approval for a standard cleaning in most cases. Check your own HOA notes if you have questions, and tell us if there are access hours we should follow.
